s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue on MRI
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Motion of the right limb joint is slightly limited
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings include normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining was negative

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the unilateral, progressive skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by localized scleroderma, which aligns with the skin hardening and hyperpigmentation

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less specific, scleroderma is a plausible diagnosis given the skin and joint findings

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the skin hardening and limited joint motion, especially with the increased expression of CD34

shortlist.label: Scleroatrophic syndrome of Huriez
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that could account for the progressive skin hardening and joint involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and the absence of inflammation, is most consistent with Linear Scleroderma. The condition typically presents in childhood and can cause limited joint mobility due to skin hardening.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: While Morphea can cause skin hardening, it typically presents with multiple lesions and does not usually cause joint limitation.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a systemic disease that typically presents with bilateral and symmetrical skin involvement, which is not consistent with this patient's unilateral presentation.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic Fasciitis is characterized by rapid onset of skin hardening and inflammation, which is not consistent with this patient's 7-year history of progressive skin hardening and lack of inflammation on histopathology.

rejected.label: Scleroatrophic syndrome of Huriez
rejected.why: Scleroatrophic syndrome of Huriez is a rare genetic disorder that presents with scleroatrophic skin changes, but it is typically associated with other features such as nail dystrophy and palmoplantar keratoderma, which are not mentioned in this case.
